first.rationale: Onboarding completion and activation are both declining, and prior evidence indicates shorter onboarding improved completion and time-to-value. Promotional pricing may address competitive SMB pressure, but prior evidence flags a material 30-day retention decline, creating downstream-value risk against the sustainable qualified-revenue objective. Verify both records before committing and run a guarded onboarding simplification test rather than assuming the prior lift fully transfers to current conditions.

final.rationale: Run a standard experiment simplifying onboarding. The verified prior result showed completion up 13%, time-to-value 2.1 days faster, and 30-day retention up 3%, directly addressing both current onboarding-completion and activation declines while supporting durable qualified revenue. Do not use promotional pricing: although it improves acquisition, its verified 12% 30-day-retention decline makes it unsuitable for the primary objective. Measure qualified activation, time-to-value, and retention by segment before any broader rollout.
